column1: # THE FORGIVING REFERENCE -- maybe, and the absence it answers with.
# A path that names nothing is `no_path`, and that is right: a typo
# should be loud. But a document that reads OPTIONAL input has no way
# to say "if it is there" -- the miss refuses the whole call, so
# `each($.tags, t)` cannot be written against a record that may carry
# no tags. `maybe(v)` is that way: the value when it resolves, and
# ABSENCE when the only thing wrong is that it is not there.
# EVERY EXPECTATION HERE WAS OBTAINED BY RUNNING BOTH ENGINES AND
#   ABSENCE GENERATES NOTHING, and generation drops it at a REQUIRED
#   key as readily as at an optional one (maybe-map-drops-key), and
#   from a list without leaving a hole (maybe-list-leaves-no-hole).
#   That is the whole difference from any, which is not generable and
#   ABSENCE PROPAGATES THROUGH A CALL: a call on an absent argument is
#   no call, in any argument position (maybe-join-separator,
#   maybe-add-operand) and for every builtin, which is why the rule
#   lives in the shared function machinery rather than in each verb.
#   ABSENCE IS THE UNIT OF THE MEET, on EITHER side: `&` dispatches on
#   its left operand, so maybe-unit-left and maybe-unit-right are two
#   ONLY A MISSING REFERENT IS FORGIVEN. A conflict inside the argument
#   is the document's own bug and is reported where it happened
#   IT WAITS FOR THE MODEL. maybe-forward-reference answers the value,
#   not absence: a reference that has not resolved YET is not a
#   reference to nothing, and `maybe` fires only once the model has
#   settled -- the staging every constructor in the language uses.
